clue.text: Fiendish advice for young Gobho

parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice the servant Launcelot Gobbo hears the fiend at his elbow urging him to shift himself and run away from his master

explanation.surface: A question about what devilish counsel was given to a young man named Gobbo.
explanation.walkthrough: Launcelot Gobbo, the clown in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, debates with his conscience and the fiend; the fiend's word to him is 'budge', meaning move off.
explanation.definitionFit: The fiend's urging to Launcelot Gobbo is literally this one-word instruction to shift or move away.

clue.text: Colleague bellowed loudly when drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person's speech is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A co-worker shouted noisily after having too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges BELLOWED plus F (forte, loudly).
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is an associate or ally, someone you are closely linked with in a venture.

clue.text: Possibly divine underworld spring

parts.note: 'divine' looks like holy, but it is the verb for seeking water with a forked rod, perhaps to find a spring underground

explanation.surface: A sacred fountain in the land of the dead, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water using a rod, which is water divining.

clue.text: In Eire, nice means peaceful

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: In Ireland, being pleasant amounts to being calm.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Eire, nice'; 'means' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eirenic (from Greek eirene, peace) means aiming at peace or reconciliation, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Large store displays the lever tin-opener

indicators.note: a tin-opener is something that goes into a tin, so these words are pushed inside the tin

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a bar is a lever, as in a crowbar

explanation.surface: A big shop shows off a tin-opener with a lever action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' works on 'tin': THE and BAR (lever) go into TIN, TI...N, giving TI-THEBAR-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn was a great barn where a parish's tenth share of produce was stored for the church.

clue.text: Garment with funny leg holds the eye

parts.note: a tog is an item of clothing, as in togs

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the word leg is jumbled

explanation.surface: An outfit with a comical leg that catches the attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds the eye' sounds like attracting attention, but describes a peg fastener passed through a loop or eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A toggle is a short bar fastener that is pushed through a loop to hold a coat closed.

clue.text: This instruction may be titular — nothing in it

indicators.note: in it puts the zero inside the rearranged word
may be says the word could become something else, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: This guidance might be just in name, with no substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges TITULAR to TUTRIAL; 'in it' puts O (nothing) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a session or text of teaching, so it is a kind of instruction.

clue.text: Isle of stone

parts.note: Ireland's poetic name links it with a green gemstone

explanation.surface: An island made of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is called the Emerald Isle for its green fields, and an emerald is a precious stone.

clue.text: Next one in a scalene triangle

explanation.surface: The following example in a lopsided three-sided figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next one' reads as a phrase, but splits into two definitions; a scalene triangle has three unequal sides, so one is the long side.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside or next to, and a scalene triangle, all sides unequal, has one longest edge.

clue.text: Relative to the point, in particular

indicators.note: in says the compass point sits within the word for particular

parts.note: nice means fussy or particular
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Something pertinent and specific in its detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the point' looks like a phrase meaning relevant; 'to' is a link and 'the point' is E.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece, a sibling's daughter, is a family member.

clue.text: A straightforward county side

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
right is one side, as opposed to left

explanation.surface: A frank and honest team representing a county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; 'county side' suggests a sports team, but it splits into the county and a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright describes someone blunt and plain-spoken, so it is a synonym for frank and direct.

clue.text: Rib woman about approval for call up

indicators.note: about means going round, so the woman's name surrounds the word for approval

parts.note: in Genesis, Eve was made from Adam's rib
OK is a sign of approval

explanation.surface: Someone teases a woman about getting the go-ahead to summon someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' looks like a verb meaning tease; it points to Eve, made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon up a memory or feeling, so it is a synonym of 'call up'.

clue.text: Unchanging figure -one divided over two

parts.note: something unchanging lasts for ever, eternal
a triangle is a geometric figure

explanation.surface: A geometric shape that never alters, in which a single item is shared between a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a love affair of three people, one person torn in affection between two lovers.

clue.text: Folly, not applicable in Miss Locket's case

indicators.note: in, with case, tells us the abbreviation sits inside the girl's name

parts.note: Lucy Locket is the girl in the nursery rhyme who lost her pocket
NA is the usual abbreviation for not applicable on forms

explanation.surface: A foolish act that has no bearing on Miss Locket's lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucy Locket lost her pocket' is an English nursery rhyme; 'in ... case' puts NA inside LUCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunacy means madness or extreme foolishness, so it serves as a synonym for folly.

clue.text: On which to get a letter from Peter Pan with love?

definitions.text: On which to get a letter from Peter Pan with love?

indicators.note: from says the letters are made out of the name, rearranged

parts.note: O, zero, is love in tennis

explanation.surface: Asking what stationery a note from the boy who never grew up, signed with love, arrives on.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PETER PAN plus O (love) are rearranged; the whole clue also describes what a letter is written on.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepaper is writing paper for letters, the material a letter from anyone arrives on.

clue.text: Perhaps dishy, and certainly keen on clothes

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words could be in another order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who might be attractive and is definitely interested in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges the letters of DISHY and AND; 'certainly' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man devoted to smart dress, so the adjective means fond of fine clothing.

clue.text: Not the kind of carriage Richard wanted

definitions.text: Not the kind of carriage Richard wanted

parts.words: Not the kind of carriage Richard wanted
parts.note: Shakespeare's Richard III cries 'my kingdom for a horse!', so he wanted one, not a motor car once called a carriage without one

explanation.surface: A comment on a carriage Richard did not want.
explanation.walkthrough: Early cars were 'horseless carriages'; at Bosworth Shakespeare's Richard III, unhorsed, desperately wanted a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'horseless carriage' was the early name for the motor car; without a mount, Richard was exactly that.

clue.text: Made a moving cartoon full of life

explanation.surface: Someone produced a lively, touching cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated describes a drawn film given motion, and also someone lively and spirited.

clue.text: Often a sign of a sticking point

definitions.text: Often a sign of a sticking point

parts.words: Often a sign of a sticking point
parts.note: a sticking point sounds like a snag in negotiations, but here it is a freshly decorated spot that will stick to your fingers, flagged by a notice

explanation.surface: A remark about how a deadlock in talks is commonly indicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice warning of fresh decorating marks a surface that is still tacky to the touch.

clue.text: Shorten a contract, maybe

parts.note: contract bridge is a card game, so bridge is an example of a contract game

explanation.surface: Cut back an agreement, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like an agreement, but it is the card game contract bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down to a shorter version.

clue.text: The course to gallop

explanation.surface: A racecourse is where horses run at full speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's course through working life, and to career is to rush along headlong.

clue.text: He's on his metal, surely, when looking for impurity

definitions.text: He's on his metal, surely, when looking for impurity

parts.words: He's on his metal, surely, when looking for impurity
parts.note: 'on his metal' puns on being on one's mettle: this tester works on metal ore, checking its purity

explanation.surface: A man determined to do his best while searching for flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: An assayer tests metals and ores to find how pure they are.

clue.text: Again fixes up for marksman to appear

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to repin is to fix again with pins

explanation.surface: Re-pinning things so that a sharpshooter can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REPINS round in this down clue; 'for' and 'to appear' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a hidden sharpshooter firing from concealment.

clue.text: Send nuts round, some to supply the emporium

indicators.note: round means the first piece wraps around the next

parts.note: to dement is to drive someone mad, to send them nuts
part means some of something
a store is a supply kept in reserve

explanation.surface: Instructions to post nuts around so that some reach a big shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like an anagram signal, but 'Send nuts' means drive mad, DEMENT, which goes round PART; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store is a large shop selling many kinds of goods, which is what an emporium is.

clue.text: Get down from vehicle — and see the composer doesn't go full length!

indicators.note: not running the full length means the name is cut short at its end

parts.note: Claude Debussy was a French composer

explanation.surface: Climb off the bus and watch the composer not finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Debussy's name stops short, losing its last two letters, SY; 'and see the' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To debus is to alight from a bus or military transport, the counterpart of embark.

clue.text: Love to scold or harangue

parts.note: O, zero, is love in tennis
to rate is an old verb for scold

explanation.surface: Love to tell off or lecture someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a choice of meanings but is a link; RATE is an old word for scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a long pompous speech, which is to harangue.

clue.text: Stand with double-bass, we hear

parts.note: read 'bass' as its soundalike 'base': a support resting on a doubled foot, that is, two legs

explanation.surface: A music stand set up beside a double bass, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works on the clue, not the answer: 'double-bass' is heard as 'double base', a stand on two feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipod is a two-legged support, as used to steady a rifle or camera.

clue.text: Sweet that helps to make a high tea?

definitions.text: Sweet that helps to make a high tea?

parts.words: Sweet that helps to make a high tea?
parts.note: high tea is a meal, but 'high' can mean drunk: this pudding is soaked in sherry or wine, so it makes the tea party merry

explanation.surface: A dessert that is a useful part of the early-evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy cake is a trifle-like pudding of sponge steeped in alcohol, a sweet course.

clue.text: Hand over old country retreat with present

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the word for the old country is read backwards

parts.note: Rus was the medieval state from which Russia grew
to render is to present or give

explanation.surface: Give up an old rural hideaway along with a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for a hideaway; it turns RUS into SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or yield something to another, to hand it over.

clue.text: Drums for dances

explanation.definitionFit: Reels are cylinders for winding cable or thread, and also lively Scottish folk dances.
